[[Deep North]] |Snow-capped hills and forests with frozen rivers, inhabited by [[Moose]], [[Elaking]], and [[Gammeltroll|Gammeltrolls]]. |Northern edge of the world |} == Alternative biomes == Each biome patch has a chance to have modifiers applied to it on world generation, but only a certain distance from the world center. These modifiers can have the following effects: * Affect foliage, like more [[Raspberries]] or only [[Birch]]es in the Meadows, or only stubs in the Black Forest * Generate additional structures, like [[Large Bone]]s in the Swamps, Plains or Mistlands, or more [[Tar Pit]]s in the Plains * Increase the chance for [[creature level|starred]] creatures * Enable the spawning of certain creatures not normally encountered in the biome, such as [[Bat]]s in the Swamp, or increase existing chances for a creature to spawn, like more [[Abomination]]s * Disable the spawning of creatures native to the biome Several modifiers can affect a single area at once. The following biomes can be affected: * [[Meadows#Alternative biomes|Meadows]] has 8 modifiers. * [[Black Forest#Alternative biomes|Black Forests]] have 8 modifiers. * [[Swamp#Alternative biomes|Swamps]] have 5 modifiers. * [[Mountain#Alternative biomes|Mountains]] have 3 modifiers. * [[Plains#Alternative biomes|Plains]] have 5 modifiers. * [[Mistlands#Alternative biomes|Mistlands]] have 6 modifiers. Oceans, the Ashlands and the Deep North do not have any alternative variants. ==Trivia== *The term "biome" comes from the [[wikipedia:biome|ecological concept of the same name]]. *At ''Valheim's'' early access launch in February 2021, five of the planned nine biomes were made available to explore. The other four were accessible, but lacked any meaningful content. ** As of the full release in September 2026, all biomes excluding the Ocean are fully implemented. An Ocean overhaul was ultimately abandoned, with the argument that it only serves the role of a highway between other biomes, which do have meaningful content. * Alternative biomes were introduced in the [[1.0]] release. {{Biomes}} [[de:Biom]] [[ru:Биомы]] [[pt-br:Biomas]] [[uk:Біоми]] [[cs:Biomy]] [[zh-tw:生物群落]] [[Category:Biomes| ]]

{{infobox biome | title = Swamp | image = Biome swamp.png | caption = | passive = * [[Giant Herring]] | hostile = * [[Blob]] * [[Oozer]] * [[Draugr]] * [[Draugr Elite]] * [[Leech]] * [[Skeleton]] * [[Surtling]] * [[Wraith]] * [[Writhan]] * [[Abomination]] | boss = [[Bonemass]] | unique = * [[Ancient Bark]] * [[Scrap Iron]] * [[Guck]] * [[Turnip Seeds]] | regular = | food = | structures = * [[Geyser]] * [[Abandoned Hut]] * [[Swamp Runestone Tower]] * [[Inverted Tower]] * [[Swamp Grave]] * [[Shipwreck]] | dungeons = [[Sunken Crypts]] | npcs = [[The Bog Witch]] }} The '''Swamp''' is an oppressive [[Biomes|biome]], filled with massive trees, muddy bogs, and hostile creatures. Immense, bare-branched [[Ancient Tree|Ancient Trees]] claw at a sickly cloud-laden sky, making for intimidating vistas. On what small bit of ground exists, tendrils of sodden soil snake around and through the knee-deep, plague-ridden water that permeates the entire biome. [[Draugr]] stumble about everywhere, watching and waiting to slay any living Viking they can find; to prove they are worthy of ascension to gods that have long since stopped listening. From a difficulty standpoint, the Swamps were designed to be a wall of sorts. Entering the biome for the first time, Vikings are met with an unprecedented drive by the very land to kill them as quickly and effectively as possible: every last creature here is hostile to the player. It is always raining in the mire regardless of the weather elsewhere; this means the player will always be [[Wet Effect|Wet]] when traversing the terrain. The toll taken on stamina in the Swamp is brutal, especially at night, when the player will also be [[Cold Effect|Cold]], and likely on the run from [[Wraith|Wraiths]]. The presence of [[Poison]] is undeniable as well, being the weapon of choice for [[Oozer]]s, [[Blob]]s, and [[Leech]]es. Making express use of a certain [[Poison Resistance Mead|mead]] unlocked in the previous biome is not negotiable. Sprinkling the landscape of any moderately large Swamp are [[Sunken Crypts]], which require a [[Swamp Key]] to unlock. These crypts sit in a state of near ruin, their winding corridors caved in and blocked by [[Muddy Scrap Pile]]s, which can be mined for [[Scrap Iron]], [[Leather Scraps]], and [[Withered Bone]]s. Up on the surface, half-submerged abandoned structures and [[Monster Spawner|hostile creature spawners]] can be found, as well as the occasional [[Geyser|Surtling Geyser]]. In addition to the Crypts, scrap piles can be found buried in the ground here. These waterlogged veins can be located using a [[Wishbone]] after defeating [[Bonemass]], though it should be noted that they tend to be uncommon and are generally not viable for providing any significant quantities of iron. Additionally, mining is a noisy activity and will attract the local fauna. == Creatures == ==== Hostile ==== * {{Item link|Blob}} * {{Item link|Oozer}} * {{Item link|Draugr}} * {{Item link|Draugr Elite}} * {{Item link|Leech}} * {{Item link|Skeleton}} * {{Item link|Surtling}} * {{Item link|Abomination}} * {{Item link|Wraith}} (night only) * {{Item link|Writhan}} * {{Item link|Seeker}} (at night after [[The Queen]] is defeated) * {{Item link|Charred Warrior}} (at night after [[Fader]] is defeated) * {{Item link|Charred Marksman}} (at night after [[Fader]] is defeated) ==== Passive ==== * {{Item link|Giant Herring}} == Resources == * {{Item link|Ancient Bark}} * {{Item link|Scrap Iron}} * {{Item link|Guck}} * {{Item link|Thistle}} * {{Item link|Turnip Seeds}} * {{Item link|Wood}} * {{Item link|Stone}} * {{Item link|Mushroom}} * Chests: (2-3 of the following) {{loot table| {{loot row|item=Amber |amt=1-5 |rate=11.8%}} {{loot row|item=Amber pearl |amt=1-3 |rate=11.8%}} {{loot row|item=Ancient bark |amt=20-30 |rate=11.8%}} {{loot row|item=Chain |amt=1 |rate=11.8%}} {{loot row|item=Coins |amt=20-60 |rate=11.8%}} {{loot row|item=Ironhead arrow |amt=10-15 |rate=11.8%}} {{loot row|item=Poison arrow |amt=10-15 |rate=11.8%}} {{loot row|item=Ruby |amt=1-3 |rate=11.8%}} {{loot row|item=Withered bone |amt=1 |rate=5.9%}} }} ==Alternative biomes== In addition to the regular [[Biomes]] generation, each local patch of biome has a chance to get an [[Alternative biomes]]. Once a Swamp is located, it is recommended that an adjacent [[Meadows]] or [[Black Forest]] is chosen for landfall. This way, it is significantly easier for a forward base to be erected and operated from. * There are various ways to glitch (i.e. through unintended ways) into a swamp crypt without using a key. These methods may be patched in later versions of the game. ** A popular strategy is to place a [[Chairs|chair]] just in front of the crypt entrance, sit in the chair, and then stand up. The player will be pushed through the gate and by extension, the loading barrier. ** The method listed above can also be utilized if a crypt is found to have an indestructible ancient tree blocking the entrance. == Gallery == Swamp1.jpg Swamp2.jpg Swamp Spawner.jpg Crypt 1.jpg Gravenimage.jpg|One of the statues found in the Swamp. He appears as a towering humanoid tree-like entity with multiple thin branches sprouting out of his slender, bark-covered body. == Summoning == [[File:TheElderAltar.png|left|thumb|200x200px|The Elder's Forsaken Altar.]] The Elder's [[Forsaken Altars|Forsaken Altar]] is located in [[Black Forest|Black Forests]]. His location can be revealed when visiting [[Burial Chambers]] and sometimes ruined structures around Black Forests, where a [[Runestone|Vegvisir]] will reveal his nearest summoning location on the map. He is summoned by placing three {{Item Link|Ancient Seed}}s in his Forsaken altar in Black Forests. Like all bosses, the Elder can be summoned as many times as desired, provided the required materials are met. == Attacks and abilities == {{For|strategies for defeating the Elder|Boss strategies#The Elder}} The Elder has an environment aura that removes darkness and raining. === Root Spawn === The Elder will raise an arm in the air to summon 15 hostile [[Root (creature)|Roots]] within a 15-meter radius circle around the player. Roots can attack players in melee range but are otherwise immobile and will despawn after 18–20 seconds or when The Elder is defeated. Although not typically possible in regular gameplay, a maximum of 30 Roots can be active at once. This ability has a 25-second cooldown and can be used while within 30 meters of a player. === Shoot === A ranged volley of 25 vines directed at a target player (35 [[Damage types#Pierce|Pierce]], 20 Tier 0 [[Damage types#Chop|Chop]] and 20 Tier 0 [[Damage types#Pickaxe|Pickaxe]] damage per hit). This attack has a 6-second cooldown and can be used when a player is 15–50 meters away. He attempts to track players while aiming. Each vine has an initial velocity of 30 meters per second and a spread of 10–20 degrees. They can travel for up to 6 seconds before disappearing. === Stomp === A close-range stomp over a large area (60 [[Damage types#Blunt|Blunt]], 1000 Tier 0 [[Damage types#Chop|Chop]] and 1000 Tier 0 [[Damage types#Pickaxe|Pickaxe]] damage). It hits in a circle 5 meters in radius from the impact point. This attack can be used when within 3 meters of a player and is accessible every 5 seconds. == Aftermath == Defeating the Elder allows the player to unlock and enter swamp crypts (which are the primary source of [[Scrap Iron]] in the game) with the [[Swamp Key]]. === Drops === {{drop table|{{drop row|item=The Elder trophy|0star=1}} {{drop row|item=Swamp key|0star=1 per player}} |stars=0}} === Forsaken power === Mounting The Elder’s trophy upon his respective stone will allow the player to claim his Forsaken Power. (if [[Bonemass]] has not been defeated) * Enables: "The ground is shaking." (if a [[Troll]] has died in the world) === Creature spawning === Defeating The Elder unlocks several creatures to spawn at '''night''' in unusual biomes. The '''Charcoal Kiln''' is used to create [[Coal]] from wood. It converts single units of [[Wood]], [[Finewood]], or [[Corewood]] into coal at a rate of 1 every 15 seconds.

It can hold up to 25 wood at a time. When adding wood to the kiln, the game will prioritize wood from the player inventory in the following order:
# Wood
# Finewood
# Corewood

== Building ==
The Charcoal Kiln is unlocked when the player acquires a [[Surtling Core]]. A nearby [[Workbench]] is required to construct it.

Kilns can be placed directly onto terrain and stone structures. Currently, they cannot be placed on wood structures, but it is possible to bypass this to an extent by terraforming terrain with a [[Hoe]] to be in line with wooden floors.

== Notes ==
* Like other structures that process materials, Charcoal Kiln are sped up with the passage of time that happens when the player is sleeping.
* When destroyed with a [[Hammer]] or other means, it drops all materials used. It is therefore possible to alternate between using a [[Smelter]] and the Charcoal Kiln, reconstructing them as needed.
* Active kilns grant the [[Fire Effect]], providing players with heat as well as scaring away the appropriate monsters, albeit only 2 meters from all sides of it (not just the interaction point).

The '''Deep North''' is a vast, snowy [[Biomes|biome]], found in the northernmost part of ''Valheim''. Described as a "postcard of a Christmas landscape", it contrasts the hordes of the fiery [[Ashlands]] with fewer but stronger creatures.

Akin to the Ashlands, the Deep North landmass is separated from other biomes by an [[Ocean]] and borders the [[World Edge]] on the northern side. There is no equivalent of the boiling sea preventing access to the biome, however, defeating [[Fader]] is still required to progress through the biome, and strong enemies pose a threat. Sheets of ice float along the shores, a potential danger to any ship attempting to dock here.

As in the Mountains, all weather in the Deep North is freezing, day and night, so players without frost resistant clothes or [[Frost Resistance Mead]] in effect take continuous [[Freezing Effect|freezing]] damage outdoors. See [[#Weather|Weather]] below.

The biome was the focus of the [[Version history|1.0 update]].

Wind intensity is capped at 1. A blizzard's wind range lies above that cap, so the wind always blows at full strength during a blizzard.

A player outdoors and away from a fire gets the [[Freezing Effect|Freezing]] effect: no health regeneration, 60% slower stamina and eitr regeneration, and one point of damage every second. Near a fire or in shelter, the player gets the [[Cold Effect|Cold]] effect instead (50% slower health regeneration, 25% slower stamina and eitr regeneration), and a fire in shelter removes both. Slight, normal or very high frost resistance prevents both effects.

While it snows, snow builds up on structures that have no roof above them and are not inside a [[Shield Generator]]'s shield. It can be cleared with the [[Snow Shovel]].

The '''Blast Furnace''' is a structure used to process advanced raw metals into ingots. Although it performs a similar function to the [[Smelter]], it cannot smelt the ores that the Smelter can.

== Building ==
It is unlocked after the player has killed [[Moder]] and built an [[Artisan Table]].

Blast Furnaces can be placed directly onto terrain and stone structures. Currently, they cannot be placed on wood structures, but it is possible to bypass this to an extent by terraforming terrain with a [[Hoe]] to be in line with wooden floors.

Unlike the Smelter, Blast Furnaces have both of their refueling ports to the left of the bar chute.

== Usage ==
The Blast Furnace is used to process certain raw materials into [[metal]] using {{Item link|Coal}} as fuel. Materials that can be smelted are:

The Blast Furnace uses 1 {{Item link|Coal}} every 15 seconds as fuel. It takes 30 seconds<ref><small>Ores used to take 31 seconds to smelt, but this was fixed in [https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/892970/view/3220644827970865344 update 0.208.1].</small></ref> to produce one bar of [[metal]].

It can hold a total of 20 Coal and 10 ores.

== Notes ==
* Like other structures that process materials, Blast Furnaces are sped up with the passage of time that happens when the player is sleeping.
* The Blast Furnace, while active, gives off the [[Fire Effect]] for about 3 meters from any side (not just the interaction point).

'''Bows''' is a [[Skills|skill]] related to the [[Bows]] weapon class.

==Effects==
Higher skill level in bows reduces the [[Stamina#Attacking|stamina]] cost to attack down to -33%, uses a random damage and knockback multiplier ranging from 25–55% at skill level 0 to 85–100% at skill level 100, and reduces draw duration up to -80% at skill level 100.

For the details of damage scaling, see [[Damage mechanics#Skill factor]].

==Notes==
* The player gains 1.5 [[Skills#Progression|xp]] per arrow when hitting a creature.
* Besides increasing damage as all weapon skills, higher levels lower the stamina draw, but also hugely reduce the draw duration, which significantly increases the fire rate and thus damage output of bows.
* [[Crossbows]] are considered a separate weapon class from bows and have [[Crossbows (skill)|their own respective skill]].

Almost every entity, object, or structure utilizes this system in some way. __NOTOC__ ==Damage types== *Physical **[[Damage#Blunt|Blunt]] **[[Damage#Pierce|Pierce]] **[[Damage#Slash|Slash]] *Elemental **[[Damage#Fire|Fire]] **[[Damage#Poison|Poison]] **[[Damage#Frost|Frost]] **[[Damage#Spirit|Spirit]] **[[Damage#Lightning|Lightning]] *Terrain **[[Damage#Chop|Chop]] (Woodcutting) **[[Damage#Pickaxe|Pickaxe]] (Mining) **[[Damage#Pure|Pure]] ==Resistances and weaknesses== {{See also|Resistance}} Resistances and weaknesses determine how much damage is taken from different [[damage types]]. [[Creatures]] have innate resistances and weaknesses but are also affected by some [[status effects]]. Players may acquire resistances and weaknesses from [[armor]], [[Mead|meads]] or [[status effects]]. The brood spawners have a 100% chance of hatching into Seeker broods, while the Seeker spawners have a 33% chance of hatching into Seekers and a 67% chance of hatching into Seeker Broods. A maximum of four Seeker broods and two Seekers can active from within a 50-meter radius of each hole - if this cap is reached the holes will not spawn any creatures. This ability is restricted to the [[Infested Citadel]] and she can still attempt to use it regardless of spawn caps. This ability has a 60-second cooldown, can be used when a player is within 25 meters, and is accessible while The Queen is below 99% health. === Spit === The Queen shoots 20 projectiles at the player which inflict the [[Poison]] and [[Slimed Effect|Slimed]] status (40 [[Damage types#Blunt|Blunt]], 40 [[Damage types#Poison|Poison]], 50 Tier 3 [[Damage types#Chop|Chop]] and 50 Tier 3 [[Damage types#Pickaxe|Pickaxe]] damage). She can use this ability every 20 seconds when within 5–25 meters of a player and while below 80% health. === Slap === Within 9 meters of a player, The Queen swings one of her arms in front of her (130 [[Damage types#Slash|Slash]], 300 Tier 3 [[Damage types#Chop|Chop]] and 300 Tier 3 [[Damage types#Pickaxe|Pickaxe]] damage). They look like huge, mutated [[Neck]]s. == Spawning == {{Spawn table|{{spawn row|type=[[Spawn zones|Middle]] of the [[Ashlands]] during the daytime|limit=2|frequency=4|stars=Yes (max 1 star)}} {{spawn row|type=[[Spawn zones|Middle]] of the [[Ashlands]] during the nighttime, despawn at dawn|limit=2|frequency=4|stars=Yes}}}} == Attacks and abilities == {{For|strategies for defeating Asksvin|Aggressive creature strategies#Asksvin}} Both before and after taming, Asksvin take no damage from [[lava]], despite not being immune to fire damage. === Bite === Sweeps their head back before rounding forward to chomp down on the player (75 [[Damage types#Blunt|Blunt]], 75 [[Damage types#Slash|Slash]], 50 Tier 0 [[Damage types#Chop|Chop]] and 50 Tier 0 [[Damage types#Pickaxe|Pickaxe]] damage). The attack does high damage to [[Grausten Structures|grausten]] and weaker structures, similar to a Lox, and it can even damage [[Factions|allied creatures]]. == Aftermath == Defeating Asksvin allows the player to loot the following items. === Drops === {{Drop table|{{drop row|item=Asksvin trophy|0star=10%|1star=10%| 2star=10%}} {{drop row|item=Asksvin bladder| 0star=1|1star=2| 2star=4}} {{drop row|item=Asksvin hide| 0star=2|1star=4| 2star=8}} {{drop row|item=Asksvin tail| 0star=2|1star=4| 2star=8}}}} Parts for a buildable [[Asksvin Skeleton]] can also be found separately in the [[Ashlands]], but they drop from destroying Asksvin Skeletons already there, not from killing Asksvin. == Taming == ''For general taming information and strategies, see [[Taming]].'' This can be prevented by either (A) trapping them in a pit or pen that they cannot escape (and staying within 64 meters of them) or (B) by starting the taming process, after which they will never despawn. Asksvin can be tamed by feeding them [[Smoke Puff]]s, [[Vineberry Cluster]]s or [[Fiddlehead]]s. They are rideable by equipping the [[Asksvin Saddle]]. When riding an Asksvin, players cannot attack. Players riding an Asksvin can traverse lava, and neither the player nor Asksvin will take damage from the lava. Tamed Asksvin do not do friendly fire damage to players, any other tamed creatures or neutral [[Dvergr (race)|Dvergr]]. == Breeding == Asksvin can breed, provided the Asksvin is happy and well-fed with [[Fiddlehead]] or [[Vineberry Cluster]] or [[Smoke Puff]], along with there being another Asksvin within four meters, and no more than 10 Asksvin within at least 10 meters. Once the conditions are met, they will accumulate love points with one another until the pregnancy starts. Pregnancy lasts 60 seconds, checked every 30 seconds, so the egg comes 60 to 90 seconds after it starts. They then lay an [[Asksvin egg]]. The quality of the Asksvin egg is determined by the Asksvin that laid it. A quality 1 egg in the player's inventory indicates a 0-star Asksvin, quality 2 indicates a 1-star, and quality 3 indicates a 2-star. Once laid, it would take 30 minutes to hatch into Asksvin Hatchling if there is a heat source nearby (Example [[Campfire]]). If the heat source is gone or the player puts the egg into their inventory, the timer is reset. Then the Asksvin Hatchling takes 50 minutes to grow into an adult without the need of heat source. They will not breed if the cap is reached, which is 10 Asksvin in 10 meters. However, there is currently no known limit to the eggs themselves. == Trivia == * The word "Asksvin" is Swedish for "ash swine." '''Portal – Stone''' is an improved [[Portal]] which becomes available soon into the [[Ashlands]] biome. It allows players to teleport with items that Wooden portals disallow, such as [[:Category:Ores|Ores]], [[Metal]]s, [[Dragon Egg]]s, [[Hildir's Chests]] and [[Mechanical Spring]]s.

A [[Stonecutter]] is required to construct the Stone portal.

== Notes ==
* It connects to any other portal using the same naming system as [[Portal|Wood portals]] and does not need to connect to the same type of portal.
* The portal the player steps into must support the materials they want to transport, meaning that while the player can go through a Stone portal that is connected to a Wooden portal with metals in their inventory, the player cannot return through the same portal pair as the Wooden portal does not allow those same metals.
* As of the Ashlands update Patch 0.218.21, the Stone portal can now be built on all stone floors (previously only on Grausten floor).
* The Stone Portal is approximately twice as large as the wooden version, requiring an area four walls high, four 2x2 flooring tiles wide, and two 2x2 flooring tiles deep to fit.

== Tips ==
* Obtaining the materials for a Stone portal (notably [[Molten Core]]s) should be a priority after arriving in Ashlands.
** If the player did not bring [[Iron]] to construct a [[Stonecutter]], they can first build a Stone portal at base, use it to transport the Iron to Ashlands, and then build a Stone portal there.
** Thanks to Stone portals, sailing out of Ashlands is never necessary, provided the player has a portal link.

UpgradeStation (station) | location = [[Mountain]] | number = 1 | inhabitants = }} The '''Forge of Potential''' is a unique [[Point of interest]] found in the [[Mountain]]. ==Location== During world generation, up to 10 spawn locations are determined for The Forge of Potential. All spawn locations are within [[Mountain]] biomes away from their edges, each at least 400 meters apart, and at least 500 meters away from the world center. Approaching any of these locations will permanently place The Forge of Potential there, nullifying all other potential spawns. When discovered, an idol icon will appear on the world map. ==Usage== It can be used as a [[Crafting]] station to upgrade [[Weapons]], [[Armor]] and [[Tools]]. An upgrade at the Forge of Potential costs a single '''idol''' of the tier that matches the item, and no other materials. The idol is consumed regardless of the result, and unlike normal upgrades there is no maximum item level. The craft has two possible outcomes: * A 65% chance to succeed and increase the item quality by one level, notably it can increase above level 4. * A 35% chance to fail. The item is destroyed and 35% (rounded up) of the materials in the base item crafting cost plus the cost of the item's current level are returned. Above level 4, each level counts as half a level for the material cost. ==List of Idols== Idols are found in [[Loot chest]] of various points of interest of theirs corresponding [[Biomes]], and sometime in the previous or next biomes.
